narratives.title: Geopolitical Escalation Risk-Off
narratives.summary: Capital is fleeing risk assets as multi-front conflicts (Iran, Israel, Ukraine) escalate beyond controlled tit-for-tat, with actual kinetic exchanges and supply chain threats (Hormuz blockade). The market consensus underestimates the persistence and structural nature of these disruptions, driving flows into safe havens.
narratives.trade_implication: Long VIX, short SPY/Nasdaq, long gold and short-dated Treasuries; underweight EM equities and oil-sensitive currencies.

narratives.title: Oil Supply Shock Repricing
narratives.summary: Capital is repricing oil higher as the Hormuz blockade persists through Q3 2026 per EIA, with SPR releases actually signaling supply tightness rather than bearishness. Kuwait's pipeline bypass talks and Iran's retaliation confirm structural disruption, but diplomatic tracks create two-way risk.
narratives.trade_implication: Long WTI crude futures and energy equities; hedge with put spreads on oil if diplomatic progress materializes.

narratives.title: Defense Spending Acceleration
narratives.summary: Capital is rotating into defense and aerospace as multiple theaters (Iran, Israel, Ukraine) demand sustained military operations and resupply. The assassination of Russian logistics chiefs and Israeli two-front readiness signal long-term procurement cycles, not one-off events.
narratives.trade_implication: Long defense ETFs (e.g., ITA, PPA) and select prime contractors (LMT, NOC); short consumer discretionary exposed to geopolitical risk.
